question: Should `/v1/chat/completions` expose internal OpenClaw tool execution telemetry, or should it keep `tool_calls` limited to caller-supplied HTTP function tools?
rationale: Current docs and code implement a client-tool contract, while exposing internal tool calls would change a full-operator HTTP API security boundary and needs maintainer intent before implementation.

options.title: Keep Client-Tool Contract
options.body: Keep internal tools out of Chat Completions responses and clarify diagnostics/tool-inventory alternatives for users who need visibility.

options.title: Design Redacted Diagnostic Mode
options.body: Add an explicit opt-in internal telemetry surface with scope checks, redaction rules, docs, and live proof.

options.title: Request Provider Repro First
options.body: Ask for a concrete qwen payload/response if the reporter expected caller-supplied function tools rather than internal OpenClaw tools.

recommendation.title: Keep Client-Tool Contract
recommendation.body: Keep internal tools out of Chat Completions responses and clarify diagnostics/tool-inventory alternatives for users who need visibility.

likelyOwner.reason: This is a product/security-boundary choice on the Gateway OpenAI-compatible API, and recent history shows follow-up ownership on the client-tool behavior.
